name: Telfes im Stubai
kurzbeschreibung: Gateway to the Stubaital, featuring the Schlick 2000 leisure center and a charming traditional village core nestled at the foot of the Stubaier Alpen.
beschreibung:
Überblick

Telfes im Stubai is situated at an elevation of 987 meters in the front Stubaital in the district of Innsbruck-Land, roughly 15 kilometers south of the provincial capital Innsbruck. Home to approximately 1,620 residents, this delightful alpine village spreads across an expansive, sun-drenched terrace high above the Ruetz river. Benefiting from a sheltered geographical position, Telfes is widely celebrated as the sunniest village in the entire Stubaital, boasting a pleasant microclimate and unobstructed vistas of the Kalkkögel peaks, frequently described as the Dolomites of North Tyrol. Telfes combines traditional rural charm with pioneer railway history, featuring Europe's highest raptor sanctuary and the premier wellness water park StuBay.

Geschichte

Archaeological evidence confirms that human settlement on the sunny plateau of Telfes began during the Early Bronze Age around 1700 to 2000 BC. The earliest documented mention appears in a 1133 Salzburg ecclesiastical charter. For centuries, Telfes functioned as the administrative and judicial center of the Stubaital, hosting the regional district court until its relocation to Mieders in the late 17th century. The municipal coat of arms, featuring a black lynx on a golden shield, honors the medieval Knights of Karlingen. A pivotal figure in the village's cultural heritage was priest and master architect Franz de Paula Penz: Telfes was his final parish, where he designed and erected the Rococo parish church of Saint Pancras between 1754 and 1756, and where he was laid to rest. Another historic milestone was the inauguration of the Stubaitalbahn railway on July 31, 1904. Built as one of the world's first single-phase alternating current narrow-gauge mountain railways, it opened the valley to international tourism.

Anreise

Access to Telfes im Stubai is scenic and comfortable by both road and rail. Motorists take the Brennerautobahn A13 to the Schönberg/Stubaital exit and follow the B183 Stubaitalstraße six kilometers up the valley directly to Telfes. A toll-free driving route connects Innsbruck via the B182 Brennerstraße. For an unforgettable journey, travelers board the historic Stubaitalbahn (STB tramline) directly at Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof, which winds along a spectacular panoramic mountain route through Mutters and across the Telfer Wiesen meadows directly into Telfes. Additionally, VVT regional bus 590 operates every 30 minutes from Innsbruck.

Tipps

A premier highlight is the Greifvogelpark Telfes raptor park at 1,000 meters elevation: daily flight demonstrations showcase eagles, falcons, buzzards, and eagle owls soaring against the dramatic backdrop of the Kalkkögel peaks. Families and wellness enthusiasts delight in the StuBay leisure center, offering indoor adventure pools, thrilling racing slides, and expansive alpine saunas. Nature lovers must explore the Telfer Wiesen, an idyllic high-altitude plateau containing the oldest and largest larch forests in North Tyrol, famous for crocus blossoms in spring and glowing golden needles in autumn. In winter, the Schlick 2000 ski and hiking resort awaits just moments away.
